'''Ida May Schottenfels''' (December 21, 1869 – March 11, 1942) was an American [[mathematician]] and university professor.

== Education and career ==
She was a student at the [[University of Chicago]], earning a master's degree in mathematics in 1896.<ref name="Zitarelli2022">{{cite book |last1=Zitarelli |first1=David E. |author-link=David E. Zitarelli|last2=Dumbaugh |first2=Della |author-link2=Della Dumbaugh|last3=Kennedy |first3=Stephen F. |title=A History of Mathematics in the United States and Canada: Volume 2: 1900-1941 |date=2022 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |isbn=978-1-4704-6730-2 |page=20 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JPGGEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Ida+May+Schottenfels%22&pg=PA20 |language=en}}</ref> After working as a schoolteacher, she joined the [[Hunter College|New York Normal College]] as an instructor in 1901, and by 1913, she headed the mathematics department at [[Adrian College]] in Michigan.<ref>{{cite book|title= Women in the scientific search : an American bio-bibliography, 1724-1979|last= Siegel|first= Patricia Joan |publisher=Scarecrow Press|year=1985|contribution=Ida May Schottenfels|pages=216–217|contribution-url=https://archive.org/details/womeninscientifi0000sieg/page/216}} </ref> She was cited as one of the most "active" women mathematicians of the time.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Fenster|first1= Della Dumbaugh|first2= Karen|last2=Parshall |author2-link=Karen Parshall |contribution=Women in the American mathematical research community: 1891-1906 |title=The History of Modern Mathematics, Vol. 3: Images, Ideas, and Communities|publisher=Academic Press|year=1994|pages=229–261}} See Table 3, p. 241, and footnote [47], p. 256.</ref> From 1891 to 1906 she gave 17 lectures at meetings of the [[American Mathematical Society]] and published three papers. She presented her paper "On a set of generators for certain substitution and Galois field groups" at the 1904 AMS meeting.<ref name="Zitarelli2022"/>

== Research ==
In [[group theory]], Schottenfels was the first mathematician to prove that there exist two non-isomorphic [[simple group]]s of the same order, by demonstrating that there are two non-isomorphic simple groups of order 20,160.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Ida May Schottenfels |date= December 26, 1899|title=Two Non-Isomorphic Simple Groups of the Same Order 20,160 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1967281 |journal=Annals of Mathematics |volume= 1|issue= 1/4|pages= 147–152|doi= 10.2307/1967281|jstor= 1967281|access-date=|url-access= subscription}}</ref>
